summary: Binary redundancy check + verbatim cross-adapter transplant
hypothesis: The champion's main loss is redundant/overlapping question slots, and a binary "do these ask the same thing?" per-pair adapter check would be a more precise redundancy ruler than embeddings or token-Jaccard — enabling surgical slot replacement with a novel donor question from a complementary adapter rather than full regeneration.
technique: Per-pair binary redundancy verification (lever F / FActScore-style decompose-then-verify): the on-device adapter answers a local yes/no "sameInfo?" check for each question pair; any flagged redundant slot is replaced verbatim with the first binary-verified-novel question from the complementary coverage-forced donor adapter (v2b_e2), with the champion draft held as the verbatim floor everywhere no swap fires.
result: Scored 0.400 on the full-30 greedy eval (2 wins / 4 ties / 23 losses vs Sonnet, 1 refusal), a slight regression of −0.009 vs the champion (0.409) and discarded. NonRedundancy nudged 3→4 in aggregate but did not lift the headline; all other rubric dimensions held (atom 4, spec 3, cover 3, nat 4). The hypothesis was falsified: the binary sameInfo check returned FALSE on pairs the Sonnet judge explicitly labels redundant, meaning the 3B adapter is too conservative/unreliable as a semantic-redundancy detector — closing the entire decomposed-binary-verification family on this axis.
